summary_paragraph: A man with a history of systolic heart failure, COPD, and homelessness was admitted for acute shortness of breath and volume overload after his medications were stolen, leading to six days without diuretics. He presented with orthopnea, leg and abdominal swelling, and a productive cough. Elevated BNP and chest imaging confirmed heart failure exacerbation with mild pulmonary edema, and he was treated with IV furosemide followed by transition to oral torsemide 60 mg. A concurrent COPD exacerbation was managed with prednisone and doxycycline. His symptoms improved, weight decreased to near dry weight, and electrolytes remained stable. The PACT team assisted with medication security planning due to housing instability. He was discharged home with instructions to continue antibiotics and steroids, monitor daily weights, and follow up as scheduled.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
